issues: Both scenes were light-grey placeholder cards with 18–24px text and grey bars, and the frame in B held only a few grey lines
No story between A and B: nothing explained why the line leaves or why that card sits in the frame
Mid-pan the frame contained a single line and nothing else, so the camera move was hard to read
Neutral grey plus a black line with no accent, so the eye had no clear target
changes: Sand look (warm paper, ink, terracotta): the line is now an 8px square-capped, hard-cornered rule and the pen tip is the only terracotta point in the shot, so the eye follows just that dot

Scene A is an 'export poster' progress card: a 170px percentage and MB count run with the line, then hold 6f at full as it flips to 'Ready to print' with a popping check, which gives the line its reason to leave

Scene B is a Saul Bass-style cut-paper poster growing inside the 720x480 frame the line draws (rising sun, overprinted hills, heavy type), with a 120px gallery caption on the left whose baseline is the line itself
Speed is continuous at every handoff: ease-out bar fill, a zero-to-zero dash out, an in-out camera, an in-out frame close; the tip stays pinned at screen x≈1480 during the pan
World content gets horizontal motion blur from camera speed, and drafting ticks grow under the line once it passes, so even the empty middle of the pan has a speed reference
Duration 160 to 190f: the poster builds in layers after the frame closes and the last 24f hold as a finished wall poster
